title: CDC says drowning happens in seconds and is often silent
summary: CDC says drowning happens in seconds and is often silent, so the adult watching should not be on a phone.
body: CDC's drowning-prevention page says drowning happens in seconds and is often silent, and that it can happen to anyone whenever there is access to water. The supervision section says an adult watching children in or near water should skip distracting activities, including reading, using a phone, and alcohol or drugs, because drowning happens quickly and quietly. That is a US public-health description. It does not give a number of seconds, and it is not a rescue method. What to do after someone is out of the water is on the first-aid drowning cards.

sources.title: Preventing Drowning
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: US federal page, public domain. Page dated 29 September 2025. Supports the seconds-and-silent line and the no-phone supervision line.
